title: Orchestrated flight plan for API/Console/Runtime release train
creator: Maya S. Reynolds
description:
Objective: define and run a coordinated release train for the API, Console, and Runtime components that minimizes customer disruption while delivering committed features. This ticket is the canonical plan for milestones, cut criteria, release notes coordination, and cross-team GTM tasks for the 2026-Q1 train.

Scope: API surface changes (minor breaking and additive), Console UI flows for rollout controls, Runtime performance improvements and a quantization profile. Non-goals: major schema rewrites, billing model changes.

Success metrics: 1) Zero P0 incidents in first 72h post-GA, 2) Release notes fully published and translated within 24h of GA, 3) Customer-facing latency SLOs met for 99th percentile within 7 days, 4) Feature adoption signals (routes opt-ins) reach > 30% of internal beta cohort within 14 days.
milestones: Feature complete (code merged to next branch) — 2026-02-28
cut_criteria: No new P0 regressions open at time of cut
All critical and high security findings remediated or mitigated with compensating controls
E2E test pass rate >= 98% on release candidate for supported regions
Performance regression vs baseline: 99p latency <= baseline + 10% (or PM/ENG accepted waiver logged)
Release notes owner assigned and draft published in Confluence
Migration or compatibility notes present for any API change
Cross-team sign-offs: ENG (runtime), API, Console, QA, Docs, Support
Rollback plan documented in runbook and validated in a dry-run
release_notes_plan: Owner: Product Docs (owner: Lina Park) — consolidate inputs by 2026-03-06
Sections required: Highlights, API changes & migration notes, Console UX changes, Runtime performance changes, Known issues, Rollout timeline, How to opt-in/out
Template: use release-notes/2026-q1 template in Confluence (link below)
Translation plan: Spanish and German prioritized; vendor request by 2026-03-07
GH links: PRs must include short changelog snippets in PR description tagged 'release-notes'
QA: Docs reviewer assigned in PR and sign-off before code freeze
cross_team_dependencies: ENG-2211 (runtime kernel selection work) — must deliver quantization profile by 2026-03-01
DES-1340 (console rollout UI) — final mocks by 2026-02-23
ENG-3309 (API versioning and compatibility tests) — tests green by 2026-03-03
QA-4012 (smoke & chaos tests) — schedule test window 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-05
rollout_plan: Canary phase: 5% traffic in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for 24 hours
Observe key metrics: request error rate, 99p latency, CPU/GPU utilization, token cost delta
Automated guardrails: if 99p latency increase > 15% or error rate > 1% for 30 minutes, auto-pause and notify oncall
Stagger expansion: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48h with manual approvals at each step
Fallback model routing: default to last-stable model variant on anomalies
Customer opt-in path: feature flag per-tenant; early adopters list managed in Tracker doc
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: runtime perf regressions under long-tail sequences — Mitigation: extended e2e with long-context fixtures + do-not-freeze kernel experiments behind a flag
Risk: release notes miss migration details — Mitigation: checklist required on every PR touching API; Docs reviewer gate on code freeze
Risk: Console rollout UX not intuitive for operators — Mitigation: internal usability session 2026-02-25 and scripted runbook exercises
Risk: Dependency test flakiness delays cut — Mitigation: freeze third-party version bumps during integration window
decisions: Decision: Use staggered canary expansion instead of big-bang GA to reduce blast radius (agreed 2026-02-17)
Decision: Accept up to 10% 99p latency delta if token cost improves >= 5% and PM signs off (exception flow documented)
Decision: Release notes must include explicit 'migration required' banner for breaking changes (Docs + Legal)
acceptance_criteria: All milestone sign-offs recorded in this ticket and Confluence
Release notes published and linked in GH release description
Canary metrics within guardrail thresholds for 48 hours post-rollout expansion
Support & Account teams have received training and playbook links before GA
Rollback validated during dry-run prior to Canary start
